newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma opposition member jailed by military.
newsitem.headline: Burma opposition member jailed by military.

text.p: Burma said on Monday that it had sentenced a member of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) to four years in jail on a charge of falsifying documents.

Myo Khin, 39, NLD secretary for Yankin township in Rangoon, was arrested on May 12 and charged with fraudulently altering a family registration list and citizen registration card, the Burmese government said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
The court had passed the sentence after a week of hearings, it added.
The statement said Myo Khin's arrest and sentence had nothing to do with an NLD party gathering set for Tuesday.
The gathering is aimed at celebrating the anniversary of the NLD's landslide victory in the 1990 election which was not recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

"Myo Khin coincidently happens to be the Secretary of the Yankin Township NLD and thus being a political party member of a certain political party does not grant him the right to make any fraudulent alterations on official documents," the statement said.
NLD sources have said the SLORC has detained 193 party members and MPs to prevent them from attending the planned gathering and banned two Rangoon NLD MPs from entering Suu Kyi's house.
